newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Forest stocks, Dow drive NZ shares to higher close.
newsitem.headline: Forest stocks, Dow drive NZ shares to higher close.

text.p: * Forestry stocks strong as S&P sector up six pct overnight
* Wall Street's 103 point gain supports market
* Market seen well underpinned and ready to rise higher
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +14.96 at 2,522.30
373 +8 * NZSC cap index -0.16 at 5,198.22
352 +6 * NZMC .NZMC cap index +10.4 at 1,982.27 381 +4 * Volume NZ$72 million. Futures untraded
785 +3 * Other movers - +12 +14
A powerful performance by New Zealand forestry stocks in line with a six percent lift in the S&P pulp and paper index sent the share market higher on Wednesday.
Brokers said the market was well underpinned just below its record high and poised to make further gains so long as support continued from overseas. The Dow on Tuesday gained 103 points.
"The market is consolidating its recents gains. It's starting to price in rate gains," said Cavill White's Richard Burton.
The top 20 index closed 14.96 points higher at 2522.30 on volume of $72 million.
Fletcher Paper gained six cents to $3.52 and Carter Holt Harvey seven to $3.72.

Brokers said news that Fletcher Canada was bracing for a long strike and CHH's parent, International Paper was planning to sell US$1 billion of assets and lay off 9000 staff were seen as seen as good for the pulp industry in the longer term.
Telecom continued its upward run, closing three ahead at $7.85.
Of the leaders, Brierley continues to be the laggard, weighed down by the poor performance of Thistle Hotels in Britain and the lacklustre listing of Bass Strait Oil which it spun off this week.
Several second line stocks performed strongly including Fletcher Building, up 12 to $4.50, Steel & Tube, up 14 to $7.05 and Air New Zealand B, up eight to $4.60.
-- Simon Louisson, Wellington newsroom, 64 4 4734 746
